doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Mother's Georgia roots and the key to Toccoa
summary: His mother was a teacher in Georgia; she was honored by her home town of Toccoa late in life.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did she ever talk to you about how she started playing, and what her influences were?
Never. Not really, you know. She was a – she was a teacher down south. You know, and when you come up north, it’s not quite as accepted to sing. She was a teacher down there in Georgia
Oh yeah. They had to – they had to have her come to Toccoa because she was the oldest – maybe the oldest person from that town.
She had to go to the court?

No, she had to go to Toccoa. It’s a town in Georgia – ‘cause she was the oldest person, she could tell them more about the town than anybody else. You know, so she was there. She went there and got the key to the town, you know.
How old were you, about, when this happened?
Oh, I don’t know. That happened…
…Were you ten? Ten years old? Older than ten?
No, no, no. That happened late.
I might have been twenty-something or something like that.
